name: manual_b3e46d
claim: When preparing a patch against a real external repository for eventual PR submission, always work from an actual git clone or fetch of that repository, never from files reconstructed via a raw-content or API fetch into a fresh git init -- matching file bytes is necessary but not sufficient, since GitHub's compare/PR view requires a real shared commit ancestor, and local checks like syntax validation or unit tests will pass even when the git ancestry itself is fabricated.

decisions.notes: 3 stacked branches prepared for upstream agentic-stack PRs were built by curl-fetching file content at a known commit SHA into a fresh 'git init' repo. The file content was byte-identical to the real commit, so every local verification (syntax check, isolated functional test) passed -- but the commits themselves had no parent and zero shared history with the real repo. GitHub's compare view correctly rejected it: 'entirely different commit histories.' Caught only because the user tried the actual link. Fixed by cloning the real fork and re-applying the same patches via git am onto genuine ancestry -- verified via the compare API afterward, not just assumed.
